design: Two fresh bug families, four repetitions of four workflows. Serial fresh isolated sessions. Per family a balanced Williams square: every arm in each position once and each ordered adjacency once within blocks. Same customer contract, observation and alphabetically ordered modules, no defect location or reference patches. Old TIDE and Python use original file+old+replacement. Named TIDE gets checked fully grouped bodies, named edit and protocol note. Named Python receives original source and accepts named multiline bodies. Tool use optional in all groups.
outcomes: Primary: within-block median (TIDE named minus TIDE text, and TIDE named minus Python named), gross tokens and end-to-end seconds, wins. Report paired Python before/after, additional old-Python comparison, reasoning/output/cache counts, regression tests and holdouts. Start before failing verification and source preparation, end after external green. Max three attempts at 180s, include failures. Four repeats nested in two bugs.
text_instruction: Find and repair the regression. You may inspect any current project source and run ./verify. Stay in the current project, preserve the public interface, and change only production code. Return JSON edits with a relative filename, a nonempty exact substring unique in that file, and its replacement. The runner applies all edits and runs ./verify. The verifier and source collection already ran. Use the prepared context directly if sufficient.
named_instruction: Find and repair the regression. You may inspect any current project source and run ./verify. Stay in the current project, preserve the public interface, and change only production code. The runner applies the submitted edits together and runs ./verify. The verifier and source collection already ran. Use the prepared context directly if sufficient.
python_guide: The reachable sources are included. Return each changed function's name and complete Python body as text, without the def line. Indentation relative to the first body statement is preserved.

dispatch.task: A router reports fast=4 and green=4 for routes (id 8, delay 2, watts 7) and (id 4, delay 6, watts 3), in that order. The fast profile must select route 8, and the green profile route 4. Fast minimizes delay, then watts. Green minimizes watts, then delay. If both values tie, the earlier input wins. Empty batches return zero IDs. All measurements are small nonnegative integers.

sources.tide/routes.tide:
record Route
id:i delay:i watts:i

initial routes:*{Route} > {Route}
case (at routes 0) (make Route id 0 delay 0 watts 0) head head
sources.python/routes.py:
def initial(routes):
    return routes[0] if routes else {"id": 0, "delay": 0, "watts": 0}
sources.tide/interactive.tide:
use routes

interactive routes:*{Route} > i
let chosen fold routes (initial routes) best row next
  if (or (< (get delay next) (get delay best)) (< (get watts next) (get watts best))) next best
get id chosen
sources.tide/eco.tide:
use routes

eco routes:*{Route} > i
let chosen fold routes (initial routes) best row next
  if (or (< (get watts next) (get watts best)) (< (get delay next) (get delay best))) next best
get id chosen
sources.tide/summary.tide:
use eco

use interactive

record Choice
fast:i green:i

choose routes:*{Route} > {Choice}
make Choice fast (interactive routes) green (eco routes)

main batches:**{Route} > *{Choice}
fold batches (list {Choice} 0) acc row batch append acc (choose batch)

tide.old: (or (< (get delay next) (get delay best)) (< (get watts next) (get watts best)))
tide.replacement: (or (< (get delay next) (get delay best)) (and (eq (get delay next) (get delay best)) (< (get watts next) (get watts best))))

tide.old: (or (< (get watts next) (get watts best)) (< (get delay next) (get delay best)))
tide.replacement: (or (< (get watts next) (get watts best)) (and (eq (get watts next) (get watts best)) (< (get delay next) (get delay best))))

press.task: A print order has two independent jobs. Job A contains colour page runs [1] and mono runs [1,1]. Job B contains colour runs [1] and mono runs [2,1]. The stock report gives 1 colour sheet and 4 mono sheets; the customer expects 2 of each. Within one job, runs of the same kind may share sheets. A colour sheet holds four pages; a mono sheet holds three. Sheets cannot be shared between jobs or kinds. Empty runs and jobs use no sheets. Counts are nonnegative small integers.

sources.tide/job.tide:
record Job
colour:*i mono:*i

pages runs:*i > i
fold runs 0 total row n + total n

sheets n:i capacity:i > i
div (+ n (- capacity 1)) capacity
sources.tide/colour.tide:
use job

colour_total jobs:*{Job} > i
let count fold jobs 0 total row job + total (pages (get colour job))
sheets count 4
sources.tide/mono.tide:
use job

mono_total jobs:*{Job} > i
fold jobs 0 total row job
  + total (fold (get mono job) 0 used run n + used (sheets n 3))
sources.tide/summary.tide:
use colour

use mono

record Stock
colour_sheets:i mono_sheets:i

stock jobs:*{Job} > {Stock}
make Stock colour_sheets (colour_total jobs) mono_sheets (mono_total jobs)

main batches:**{Job} > *{Stock}
fold batches (list {Stock} 0) acc row jobs append acc (stock jobs)

tide.old:
let count fold jobs 0 total row job + total (pages (get colour job))
sheets count 4
tide.replacement: fold jobs 0 total row job + total (sheets (pages (get colour job)) 4)

tide.old: (fold (get mono job) 0 used run n + used (sheets n 3))

python.old:
count = sum(pages(job["colour"]) for job in jobs)
    return sheets(count, 4)
python.replacement: return sum(sheets(pages(job["colour"]), 4) for job in jobs)

python.old: sum(sheets(n, 3) for job in jobs for n in job["mono"])
